title: The Imperfect
subtitle: amābam, amābās, amābat. Past continuous action.
objectives: Conjugate any verb in the imperfect active and passive.
Translate the imperfect as 'was -ing', 'used to', or 'kept on'.
Distinguish imperfect (continuous past) from perfect (completed past).
Recognize the -bā- marker in first/second conjugations and -ēbā- in third/fourth.

sections.heading: The imperfect tense
sections.body:
The imperfect describes continuous, repeated, or habitual action in the past: 'I was loving', 'I used to love', 'I kept on loving'.

First conjugation imperfect active:
  amābam, amābās, amābat, amābāmus, amābātis, amābant

The marker is -bā- (first/second conj.) or -ēbā- (third/fourth conj.).

Third conjugation imperfect:
  regēbam, regēbās, regēbat, regēbāmus, regēbātis, regēbant

Caesar writes: Gallī bellum gerēbant. — The Gauls were waging war.
Cicero writes: Catilīna coniūrātiōnem parābat. — Catiline was preparing a conspiracy.

items.prompt: Conjugate laudō in the imperfect active.
items.answer: laudābam, laudābās, laudābat, laudābāmus, laudābātis, laudābant
The soldiers were fighting / used to fight.
